key_difference: (D) adds the same RunFunctionTaskBase destructor as (B), but also rewrites how the ThreadEngine is started for map()/filter(): each start is wrapped in an auto-deleting PoolTask whose destructor cancels the future and calls threadExit() from whichever thread drops it. (B) deliberately left that path out of scope, and this adds per-start allocations, a new exported entry point and cross-thread teardown risks a maintainer would want reviewed separately.
